HeroName: Elisabeth of Bavaria, Queen of Germany
Description: Elisabeth of Bavaria was Queen of Germany and Jerusalem as consort of King Conrad IV, and mother of the tragic Conradin, later marrying Meinhard, Count of Tyrol. Weathering the catastrophic collapse of the Hohenstaufen crown, she founded Stams Abbey to mourn her executed son with royal grief. Elisabeth mourned her executed son Conradin within the quiet cloisters of Stams Abbey, defying Angevin intimidation with majestic royal fortitude in the Tyrolean peaks. Enduring the tragic execution of Conradin with unbent pride, she enshrined Hohenstaufen royal memory in Tyrolean cloisters as Europe's most revered tragic queen. Enduring the downfall of her house with holy serenity, Queen Elisabeth stood as an emblem of royal grief and unshakeable maternal dignity in the Alps. Throughout every bitter imperial diet, frontier colonization campaign, and shifting territorial conflict across Brandenburg, Carinthia, and Bavaria, their relentless aristocratic dedication, strategic statecraft, chivalric discipline, steadfast valor, and immense personal resources preserve the sovereign dignity, mercantile wealth, and military supremacy of the Holy Roman Empire, safeguarding civic liberty, territorial integrity, and dynastic grandeur against every rival prince, foreign league, and hostile coalition across Central Europe for future generations to inherit with pride, commanding profound imperial reverence from all subjects throughout Christendom and standing as an immortal beacon of chivalric honor, lawful constitutional governance, and sovereign peace across European civilization.
Motivations: Devote her life to shielding young Conradin from Angevin assassins and papal persecution.
Found Stams Abbey in the Tyrolean Alps to enshrine eternal prayers for her executed son.
Unite Bavarian and Tyrolean baronies through marriage to guard her sovereign dignity.
Values: Believes maternal courage outlasts the fall of empires, defying tyrannical conquerors.
Finds ultimate solace in sacred Christian penance, guarding royal memory amidst mountain peaks.
Fears: Her son Conradin riding to Naples against her warnings, perishing beneath the executioner's axe.
Papal wrath persecuting her surviving children and despoiling their Tyrolean sanctuaries.
SpeechStyle: Speaks with poignant royal sorrow and diamond-hard fortitude, majestic, tragic, and proud. Always fiercely defending Holy Roman imperial dignity, princely territorial liberties, and German imperial sovereignty.
